They also tend to have minimal concavity and concave points, which are more pronounced in malignant tumors. The fractal dimension and symmetry are generally less variable in benign cases, with lower fractal dimension values indicating simpler, less irregular cell structures. Adjusting these features to values typical of benign tumors—such as reducing mean radius to below 15 and lowering concavity-related metrics—significantly shifts the model's prediction from malignant (prediction 0) to benign. These changes align with established diagnostic patterns in breast cancer biomarker studies.
